basis: The Government states that Law No. 200/2025 gives the Equality Council competence to promote, monitor and support equal treatment of EU workers, answering the 2023 finding that no such body existed.
The Government states that the Equality Council acts as national contact point under Law No. 200/2025 for cooperation with Member State authorities.
The Government states that the Equality Council will restructure and increase its staff to carry out its new tasks for EU workers.
The draft law amends the Equality Council law so that the Council can carry out the tasks conferred by Law No. 200/2025.
The planned training covers equal treatment of EU workers for public authority and Equality Council staff.
The Government states that the General Inspectorate for Migration will inform Member State citizens of their rights and refer them to competent institutions.

The Government commits to apply the European Health Insurance Card, with the national health insurance company coordinating, in response to the Commission's finding that its implementation would be challenging.
The Commission reports the feasibility study on introducing the European Health Insurance Card under the card's preparation.
The Government states that a module for issuing and managing the card is being developed in the health insurance information system.
The Government states that the health care and health insurance laws must be amended to implement the card.
The draft order approves the technical specifications of the card and the provisional replacement certificate.
The Commission gives the absence of an integrated health information system as the reason no national health insurance card exists, and its 2024 key recommendation asks for that system.
The Commission states that the Agency has a mandate to develop the justice sector's information systems and their interoperability.
The Reform Agenda sets the E-File application in all first instance courts as a step towards more efficient justice.
The Commission states that the August 2026 amendments promoted the digitalisation of certain judicial procedures.
The Commission states that the new legal framework reinforced the regulator's administrative and financial independence.

The regulator's report states that with Electronic Communications Law No. 72/2025 in force from 1 January 2026 the regulator became ARCOM, and the Commission says the new framework reinforced its independence.
The regulator's report presents the BEREC working arrangements as strengthening its institutional capacity and convergence with EU practice.
The Commission records the updated infrastructure access tariffs under the Reform Agenda step on infrastructure sharing with the incumbent.
The Reform Agenda states that the incumbent will implement network-sharing agreements, responding to the minimal sharing found in the baseline.
The World Bank assessment is to give recommendations aligning the regulator's organisation with European regulator practice.
The decision amends the regulator's ex ante measures on the wholesale local access market, a competitive safeguard.
The Commission records the electronic signature for filing with the business register as progress on digital tools and processes in company law.
The Government states that Law No. 175/2021 made electronic filing for state registration of legal entities possible.
The Government states that the amendments to Law No. 220/2007 partly transpose the directive on digital tools in company law.
The draft law is titled as concerning the use of digital tools and processes in company law.

The Commission states that the new register enables registration of all legal forms and strengthens digital market entry, and the Government cites it towards transposition of the directive on digital tools.
The Government describes remote state registration of legal units as a provisional online registration service pending the new register.
The Commission records online business registration for foreign investors among digital company procedures.
The authority states that Law No. 195/2024 introduces administrative sanctions that will let it sanction breaches directly.
The training and information campaigns answer the 2023 recommendation to train public servants and raise awareness of data protection rights.
The authority prepared guidelines for the correct application of the new data protection law.
The authority states that MLog lets data subjects see who accessed their data, when and on what legal basis.
The Commission and the Reform Agenda present the new human resources management information system as the replacement for the non-functional one.
The Government links the planned integrated system for public posts and civil servants to the lack of a human resources information system.
The permits system is a shared system for issuing permits across institutions, and the Court of Accounts follows up its partial use.
The register of state information resources and systems is meant to support reuse of existing technical solutions across institutions.
The Strategy says the shared digital units will develop and operate shared platforms and services used by many organisations.
The implementation programme lists eArhiva under its objective on a unified government digital infrastructure.
The Government plans a technical solution for paperless administration across the public sector.
The Reform Agenda names the full operationalisation of the State Register of Legal Units, whose absence the baseline describes as hampering businesses.
The 2025 and 2026 key recommendations ask to finalise the digitalisation of the public property register, which the Commission reports under way.
The draft decision approves the concept of the State Population Register information system.
The State Population Register information system is a base register named in the Government's programme for modernising priority registers.
SIGMA reports a project to improve the civil status documents system, a base register still fed partly on paper.
The Reform Agenda sets a digital cadastre covering 98% of the territory, and the Government includes cadastre modernisation in it.
The Government decision approved the concept of the Real Estate Cadastre information system as the basis for its modernisation.
The Commission records the digitalisation of the business register's paper archive.
The register of state information resources and systems records state registers and their documentation, which the Court of Accounts audits.
The Government plans the modernisation, automation and interoperability of state registers.
The Commission reports that the EVO integrated portal brings together 636 public services, 447 of them online.
The Commission describes the portal as the single point of access to online public administrative services.
The Commission states that the centres were set up to respond to persistently low demand for e-services in rural areas.
The Government reports that the project digitalised and redesigned public services.
The Commission links notable progress on the digitalisation of public services to implementation of the Strategy.
The Government plans to integrate the portal with the EU Single Digital Gateway, which the Reform Agenda baseline notes is missing.
The draft amendment of the public services law is to transpose the Single Digital Gateway rules.
The Reform Agenda links expanding digital business services to life-event-based service delivery.
The Commission records the methodology on life events under the Reform Agenda step on digital services.
The Reform Agenda sets the expansion of the digital wallet to at least 20 digital public services.
The Reform Agenda aims to increase the number, quality and relevance of digital public services.
The Government customer support service is set up to support users of public services.
The Commission assesses the expired Digital Moldova 2020 strategy against its targets and reports particularly weak results on services online and their acceptance.
The Government's 2024 implementation report states that the Strategy's results in 2023 show significant progress in digitalising public services.
The Commission reports that user uptake of e-services increased significantly, including in rural areas where 118 centres were set up to respond to persistent low demand.
The e-Governance Agency's publication attributes 94 redesigned services, some with delivery time cut by 40%, to the Modernization of Public Services project.
The e-Governance Agency's publication states that use of digitalised services doubled over the Modernization of Public Services project.
The e-Governance Agency's publication states that 38% of the vulnerable population accessed digitalised services, against 6% at the start of the project.
The e-Governance Agency's publication states that savings from MPay payment fees alone recovered the 46 million dollar investment in the two projects.
The Court of Accounts states that registrations in the system confirm the establishment of an automated mechanism for registering state information resources and systems.
The regulator's 2025 report states that, through the BEREC working arrangements, it benefits from strategic information and BEREC support, strengthening its capacity and convergence.
The State Chancellery's monitoring report states that all 67 public authorities submitted their internal control reports through the platform in 2025.
